priorScientificBaseline.consumed: Previously reviewed Snell/index orientation, normal-incidence, critical/grazing distinction and model-domain context only

questions.sourceRequest: Calculate water relative to diamond and carbon disulfide relative to ice.
given: Orientation of the two relative-index requests
notGiven: A hash-bound accepted numerical table for these four materials
Wavelength, temperature or other index-measurement conditions
ambiguities: Do not substitute remembered common indices or treat old rounded examples as exact material constants.
questions.solutionRequirement: Define relative index in the requested order, using common-condition absolute indices; keep numerical evaluation HOLD unless readable accepted source-table numbers are supplied.

questions.sourceRequest: For parallel rays directed at a plane-parallel slab, find the distance x between their emergence points.
given: l=0.7 cm described as distance between rays passing through the slab
notGiven: The segment/direction along which l is measured
Whether l refers to internal or exterior rays
ambiguities: Shortest separation perpendicular to internal rays, shortest separation of exterior rays, and a separation along the surface are distinct quantities.
questions.solutionRequirement: Present only conditional projection relations with named spacing conventions. Do not supply an index, thickness, diagram or numerical x, even conditionally.

questions.sourceRequest: Give the direction of apparent displacement when observing an object through a triangular prism.
given: Observation of an object through it
ambiguities: The usual denser-prism result must distinguish physical ray deviation from the backward-projected apparent displacement; an inverse index ordering changes the sign.
questions.solutionRequirement: Derive the direction in an explicitly stated direct two-face refraction model, without assigning a source numerical index or figure geometry.

questions.sourceRequest: Can a glass prism with right-isosceles triangular base, immersed in water, be used as in Figures 161 or 162?
notGiven: Resolved internal ray incidence/arrow details for the two figures
ambiguities: Right-isosceles shape alone does not fix every ray's incidence. A conventional 45-degree internal-reflection route may be analyzed only conditionally, not asserted as an observed source path.
questions.solutionRequirement: State the TIR index/incidence condition and a separately conditional 45-degree specialization; retain the requested diagram-specific yes/no HOLD.

questions.sourceRequest: Place the same glass prism from Q4 with one short side down on newspaper; can the text be seen through the other short side or through the long side?
given: View through the other short side and the long side
notGiven: Air gap versus optical contact at the newspaper
ambiguities: The same prism fixes shape/material, not an unspoken replacement of water by air. A face name alone does not fix a normal viewing direction. Reflected paths and direct two-face transmission are different image routes.
questions.solutionRequirement: Use explicit analytic right-isosceles geometry for conditional routes; do not infer a source figure, silently add air/indices, or give an unqualified two-face yes/no answer.

questions.sourceRequest: A ray from deep water is totally internally reflected at the water surface; after cedar oil is poured on the water, can it enter air?
ambiguities: Plane parallel layers and the same incident ray must be stated as the solvable model. Nonparallel/rough boundaries can change ray direction; an evanescent field is not an escaping propagating ray.
questions.solutionRequirement: Derive conserved tangential Snell quantity through the layers, split possible first-interface regimes and handle strict TIR/grazing. No remembered cedar-oil index is permitted.

questions.sourceRequest: For an equilateral triangular prism, equal entry/exit distances from the vertex are required; find the maximum permissible material refractive index n.
given: Equal entry/exit distances from the vertex
notGiven: Whether a grazing limiting ray is admitted
Explicit direct single-pass versus internally reflected route
ambiguities: Equal positive distances on the two crossed faces of a common 60-degree vertex define the standard symmetric direct route. A bound with grazing equality is not an attained maximum for a non-grazing entering/emerging ray.
questions.solutionRequirement: Derive the internal geometry, Snell inequalities and exterior-index dependence; separate strict propagating crossing from the grazing boundary/supremum. Do not silently make air's absolute index exactly one.

globalOpticalModelPolicy: Use ordinary homogeneous isotropic transparent positive-index media and geometric ray optics unless a conditional branch states otherwise.
All incidence/refraction angles are measured from interface normals.
Use N_1 sin(theta_1)=N_2 sin(theta_2) without undefined normal-incidence sine ratios.
For N_1>N_2, strict TIR has N_1 sin(theta_1)>N_2; equality is the grazing boundary, not a finite normal-flux transmitted ray.
State finite-aperture/direct-route and medium assumptions explicitly; do not identify them with unresolved source pixels.
No source table was opened or supplied by a separate numeric binding in this batch. No remembered material-index value becomes source evidence.
